memory_update.text: US-listed pure-play exposure to high-end sub-100nm barium titanate powder for MLCCs appears weak. The most relevant upstream names found in this pass are Japan-listed or private, so US candidates should be treated as downstream/adjacent unless direct sourcing or design-win evidence emerges.

VSH is the strongest US-exchange underfollowed candidate for this node because it has official high-voltage MLCC products and a mid-cap profile, but AI-server revenue/design-win evidence remains unverified.

KN is a speculative shadow candidate: it has specialty MLCC/high-voltage capacitor capability, but current public evidence points more to defense, industrial, medtech, optical networks, telecom, and automotive than AI-server MLCC demand.

Murata and TDK should be retained as reference leaders for AI-server MLCC product requirements, while Sakai Chemical and TODA KOGYO should be tracked as non-US upstream powder comparables for the true dielectric-material bottleneck.

node: AI-server MLCCs and upstream barium titanate dielectric powders
summary: Layer 1B expansion found that the cleanest public-market exposure to the upstream barium-titanate powder chokepoint is mostly outside the US-listed universe: Sakai Chemical is TSE-listed, while Ferro/Vibrantz appears private. For US-accessible names, the list splits into OTC ADR reference leaders with direct AI-server MLCC exposure, and US-exchange underfollowed/specialty capacitor makers with plausible but not yet proven AI-server pull-through. Vishay and Knowles are not confirmed AI-server MLCC bottleneck winners; they enter as underfollowed hypotheses because they manufacture high-voltage, high-reliability, or specialty MLCC/capacitor products adjacent to the AI-server power architecture trend.
